about: Zones a city sets for shared e-scooters, read from the layers of its public map: where to park, where not to, where to ride slowly and where not to ride. Some state a licence for theirs: Alexandria, Rostock and Stockholm CC0, Basel, Braunschweig, Helsinki, Namur, Taupō, Turku, Vantaa and Wien CC BY 4.0, Berlin the Datenlizenz Deutschland – Zero 2.0, Hamburg, München and Münster the Datenlizenz Deutschland – Namensnennung 2.0, St. Albert its Open Data License, Santa Monica ODC-By 1.0, Vancouver the Open Government Licence – Vancouver, the City of London the Open Government Licence v3.0, Lambeth too for its website, and Washington CC BY 4.0 for its corrals and no-parking zones; since 28 October 2026 public city layers are drawn without one too, credited to the city. Taupō's and Namur's operations areas, where their scooters may go at all, are not drawn. Namur's zones where a scooter may be parked only in a reserved place are drawn as such, only on the website, as Helsingborg's centre, Braunschweig's old town within the Oker, the London Borough of Lambeth and Poznań's zone of Hop & Go points are. Oslo's school yards, no-riding on weekdays only, are not drawn: only its zones of every day are. Each city's zones are in data/city-zones/<id>.json, written by scripts/update-city-zones.mjs from the layers below, with the bounds here: each zone is one ring of [lat, lng] points, simplified to within half a metre, or 2 m for Berlin's, Hamburg's and München's no-parking zones and Wien's no-parking and no-riding zones, drawn to the centimetre, and 20 cm for Stockholm's parking places, one of them 70 cm wide. A zone of several parts is a zone for each, and a hole in one, as in five of Västerås's, is drawn by its ring going round the hole and back. Norrköping's map serves its zones only as pictures: they are read from the SVG it draws, to within its 0.5 m pixels for the parking places and 2.75 m for the other zones. Porto gives its parking places as points with their number of spots, so each is drawn as a disc of 5 m around its point, and so are Boise's and Arlington County's parking corrals, those installed, Seattle's bike and scooter corrals, Santa Monica's and Sacramento's drop zones, Namur's signed parking places, Poznań's Hop & Go points, Lambeth's parking bays, Ottawa's designated parking, Turku's parking places, Rostock's, Stockholm's five given as points and Hamburg's parking areas, marked or at stops; Berlin's are the circles of 10 m it draws round each of its parking places. Ottawa's no-ride roads and pathways are lines, not drawn; nor are Minneapolis's mobility hubs, no places a ride must end. Vantaa's mandatory parking zones and Vaasa's restricted parking area, where a ride may end only at one of the city's parking places, are not drawn, nor are Vantaa's temporary zones for events, nor München's areas and zones set until a day, for building sites or an event, nor Wien's set until a day or for some days only, as the Naschmarkt's flea market on Saturdays. Arlington National Cemetery is no city, but federal rules forbid riding there (32 CFR 553.33(c)(8)): it is drawn as a no-ride zone, its outline from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL), credited to both. Boulder's are Lime's, the operator's, credited to it: the City of Boulder's own layer answers scripts only with a challenge, so they are read from the public zone file Lime's rider app draws them from, each zone an encoded polyline, to within about a metre. Its mandatory parking zone, where a ride ends at a Lime corral that the file does not hold, and its two no-riding areas of about 90 km² round the city, where Lime's service area ends, are not drawn. Nagoya's zones are lines instead of a ring: the pavements where a scooter in its 6 km/h mode may ride, rule 81 (普通自転車歩道通行可) of the Aichi police's traffic rules as JARTIC publishes them, those whose middle lies within the city's outline on OpenStreetMap, simplified to within a metre. Only the website draws them; the apps' catalogs leave them out. The map draws them from zoom 14, whether or not the operators' zones are on. Berlin's and Hamburg's, too many to build into the iPhone app, are marked download: the app downloads them when a view reaches the city (docs/city-zone-downloads.md). The website draws them as it does the others.

source.title: City of Alexandria, "Dockless Mobility": its slow zones, at 6 mph, on the Old Town waterfront, the pedestrian blocks of King Street and Founders Park, and its parking corrals; its corral areas and micromobility restrictions are open data (CC0)

map.title: City of Alexandria, "Micromobile Restrictions" (open data, ArcGIS)

source.title: Stad Antwerpen, open data, "deelmobiliteit NOGO-zones": zones where riding a shared e-step is forbidden, such as cemeteries and tunnels; with its no-parking zones, such as parks and the city centre, its low-speed zones, such as the Meir, and its drop zones, where shared vehicles are preferably left

map.title: Stad Antwerpen, "deelmobiliteit_drop_zones" (open data, kept daily)

source.title: Arlington County, "Shared Micro-Mobility Devices": more than 100 corrals throughout the County, safe places to park e-scooters and e-bikes upright and out of the way of pedestrians, motorists and other road users

map.title: Arlington County, "Shared Micromobility Device Parking Corrals" (map, ArcGIS)

source.title: 32 CFR 553.33(c)(8): no one may ride a bicycle or similar conveyance in an Army National Military Cemetery, except with a pass issued to visit a gravesite or niche

map.title: Arlington National Cemetery on OpenStreetMap (relation 2475077, © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL)

source.title: City of Atlanta, Department of Transportation, "Micromobility Corrals and Racks Map": the City's and Midtown Alliance's micromobility corrals, where shared scooters and bikes park

map.title: City of Atlanta, "Micromobility Corrals" (ArcGIS)

source.title: Baltimore City Department of Transportation, "Baltimore City Bike Racks and Scooter Parking Map": its scooter corrals, for the City's shared scooter program

map.title: Baltimore City Department of Transportation, "Scooter Corrals" (ArcGIS, last updated 2024)

cities.authority: Kanton Basel-Stadt, Amt für Mobilität, CC BY 4.0

source.title: Kanton Basel-Stadt, "Shared Mobility": the map of the zones where shared micromobility may not be used (Sperrzonen, orange) or parked (Parkverbotszonen, violet), which the providers must build into their apps (Nutzungsordnung of 1 September 2025)

map.title: Kanton Basel-Stadt, "Verbotszonen geteilte Mikromobilität: Sperr- und Parkverbotszonen" (open data, dataset 100332)

source.title: Bergen kommune, "Elsparkesykler i Bergen": in the inner city centre, park only on the marked places; in no-parking zones a ride cannot end

map.title: Bergen kommune, "Elsparkesykkel i Bergen" (map)

source.title: Senatsverwaltung für Mobilität, Verkehr, Klimaschutz und Umwelt, "Elektro-Tretroller in Berlin": an e-scooter may not be ridden or parked in a park

map.title: Geoportal Berlin, "Parkverbotszonen für Mietfahrzeuge der Mikromobilität": the parks, playgrounds, cemeteries and places the districts report that rental operators keep free under their permits since 1 September 2022, and "Abstellflächen für Mikromobilitätsangebote", where riders should preferably leave them (open data)

source.title: City of Boise, "How to Use E-Scooters and E-Bikes": obey the geofence no-ride and slow zones shown on the City's map; downtown and on Boise State's campus, end the trip at a mandatory parking pin; designated parking corrals are marked "Park Here"

map.title: City of Boise, micromobility map (ArcGIS)

source.title: City of Boulder, "Shared E-scooters and E-bikes": Lime's scooters, standing and seated, are geofenced, their speed limited in places and stopped in no-go zones; in the Mandatory Parking Zone, most of central Boulder, a ride ends at a Lime parking corral

map.title: Lime's zones for Boulder, the public file its rider app draws them from

source.title: Stadt Braunschweig, press release 790/2022 of 26 October 2022: within the Okerumflut, the old town's ring of the Oker, a hired e-scooter must be parked on one of the marked parking places, or its rental runs on; under its agreement with the operators, scooters may not be parked on green spaces, by water, in the pedestrian zone and before some listed buildings

map.title: Stadt Braunschweig, "E-Tretroller | Parkverbotszonen" and "Abstellflächen für E-Scooter" (open data, CC BY 4.0)

source.title: City of London Corporation, "Parking Places (Scooters/Cycle Hire)": its parking places for hire scooters and bikes on its streets, each set by a traffic management order; open data under the Open Government Licence v3.0

map.title: City of London Corporation, "Scooters and Cycle Hire Parking Places" (INSPIRE map service, ArcGIS)

source.title: City of Columbus, Division of Parking Services, "Mobility and Parking Map": its scooter corrals among the City's parking options

map.title: City of Columbus, "Mobility and Parking Map" (ArcGIS)

cities.authority: Freie und Hansestadt Hamburg, Behörde für Verkehr und Mobilitätswende, DL-DE BY 2.0

source.title: hamburg.de, "E-Scooter in Hamburg": a rental cannot be ended in the no-parking zones the city set with the operators, shown red in their apps, and where it can, the city pairs them with marked parking areas, shown with a P

map.title: Freie und Hansestadt Hamburg, "Abstellflächen und Parkverbotszonen E-Scooter Hamburg" (open data)

source.title: Helsingborgs kommun's local traffic rule 1283 2022:502, in force since 1 September 2022: e-scooters may park on a pavement or cycle track only outside the marked area of central Helsingborg, so within it they park in a bicycle rack or a marked place

map.title: Svensk trafikföreskriftssamling (Transportstyrelsen), 1283 2022:502, its map

source.title: Helsingin kaupunki, "Sähköpotkulaudat": in the inner city (the centre, Taka-Töölö, Pasila, Kallio and Kalasatama) and near metro and train stations a rental e-scooter may be parked only in a marked parking place, painted on the ground and shown in the rental apps

map.title: Helsinki Region Infoshare, "Parking places in Helsinki" (open data, WFS)

source.title: Järvenpään kaupunki, "Sähköpotkulautojen rajoitusalueet ja pysäköintipaikat": the no-riding, no-parking and 10 km/h areas of its micromobility permit, from the 2026 season, which the operators must enforce in their apps

map.title: Järvenpään kaupunki, "Sähköpotkulautojen rajoitusalueet ja pysäköintipaikat" (web map, ArcGIS)

source.title: Lambeth Council, "Dockless Cycle Hire": Lambeth uses a bay-only parking system, so a rental e-scooter or e-bike is left in a designated dockless parking bay at the end of a journey

map.title: Lambeth Council, "Lambeth Shared E-scooter and E-bike Parking Bays" (Google My Maps)

folder: Transport for London Shared Bay Locations

source.title: City of Minneapolis, "Park a scooter": lock a scooter to a public bike rack, a parking meter hitch or most street signs, not a bus stop sign, and keep it out of the sidewalk's 4-foot clear zone; the City's geofences mark where a ride may not end (bridges, construction), where riding is illegal (pedestrian areas, construction, parking garages) and where speed is capped at 8 or 10 mph

map.title: City of Minneapolis, "SBSP_Operations_and_Geofence_Data" (ArcGIS)

source.title: München unterwegs, "E-Tretroller-Sharing": since 5 August 2022 a rented e-scooter in the old town may be returned only in a marked parking area, and none may be parked in the pedestrian zone or green spaces; the city's geoportal shows its parking areas and no-parking and no-riding zones

map.title: Landeshauptstadt München, Mobilitätsreferat, "Abstellverbotszonen für Elektrokleinstfahrzeuge" (open data)

source.title: Stadt Münster, Ordnungsamt, "Elektro-Tretroller": since 24 April 2023 the city has marked parking zones for e-scooters, first in the city centre and on Weseler Straße, and the public areas round them that are not parking zones are no-parking zones, where a rental cannot be ended

map.title: Stadt Münster, "Abstellflächen und Parkverbotszonen E-Scooter Münster" (open data)

source.title: National Police Agency, "特定小型原動機付自転車に関する交通ルール等について": on the pavements drawn, signs let bicycles ride, and so e-scooters in their 6 km/h mode (speed lamp flashing): keep to the part marked for bicycles, or else to the half nearer the road, go slowly, and stop rather than get in a pedestrian's way. Off them, ride on the road. The signs on the street take precedence over this map, such as a 特例特定原付を除く plate, which keeps scooters off (police data, August 2026). 出典：「交通規制情報」（https://www.jartic.or.jp/service/opendata/）（公益財団法人日本道路交通情報センター）を加工して作成

map.title: JARTIC (公益財団法人日本道路交通情報センター), open data 「交通規制情報」: the Aichi police's traffic rules, rule 81 普通自転車歩道通行可

source.title: Ville de Namur, "Trottinettes": in the city centre and some other zones a shared e-scooter may be parked only in a reserved place, signed on the street, or in a virtual one the operator's app shows

map.title: Ville de Namur, open data, "Namur - Mobilité - Le libre-partage à Namur": the zones set for its shared scooters and e-bikes

source.title: NYC DOT, Shared E-Scooter Program, "Frequently Asked Questions": in the East Bronx and Eastern Queens a shared e-scooter is parked upright in the sidewalk's furniture zone, or, in a mandatory corral zone, inside a designated corral to end the trip

map.title: NYC Open Data, "Shared E-Scooter Parking Corrals" (Department of Transportation)

source.title: City of Norfolk, "Micro-Mobility Program": end a ride in one of the designated parking corrals or at a bike rack, or if none is free on the sidewalk close to the curb

map.title: City of Norfolk, "Norfolk's Bike Network & Facilities Map" (ArcGIS): its existing micromobility corrals

source.title: Norrköpings kommun, "Elsparkcyklar": park in a bicycle stand or at the marked e-scooter places in the inner city; its land-use guideline has the operators keep scooters to 6 km/h in places and from being returned in the areas its map shows

map.title: Norrköpings kommun, map themes "Elsparkcyklar, begränsningar" and "P-plats elsparkcyklar" (kartor.norrkoping.se)

source.title: City of Omaha, New Mobility Hub: a scooter that enters a designated No Ride Zone is shut off automatically and must be walked out of it before the ride goes on; the City's automatic enforcement zones allow neither parking nor riding

map.title: City of Omaha, automatic enforcement zones for scooters (ArcGIS)

source.title: Oslo kommune, "Leie av elsparkesykler og elsykler": the city's map shows where e-scooters may not be left (yellow), where to park them (green), where to ride slowly (blue) and where not to ride (red), and rental operators must geofence its zones (Oslo's regulation on renting small electric vehicles, § 7c)

map.title: Oslo kommune, Bymiljøetaten, "Reguleringsbestemmelser for elsparkesykler og elsykler i Oslo kommune" (map)

source.title: City of Ottawa, "E-scooter rules and safety requirements": a shared e-scooter is parked upright in a signed designated space or an area its provider's app permits, and providers geofence no-ride, no-park and slow zones, the City's map of shared e-scooter areas showing its no-ride and slow ride zones and designated parking

map.title: City of Ottawa, "Map of shared e-scooter areas"

source.title: Øygarden kommune, "Kunngjering av løyveordning for utleige av små elektriske køyretøy på offentleg grunn i Øygarden kommune" (December 2025): rental operators must geofence the kommune's zones in Straume, from 1 March 2026 to 29 February 2028

map.title: Øygarden kommune, "Geogjerder og soneinndeling ØK" (map, ArcGIS)

source.title: echoboomer, "Polícia Municipal do Porto começou a aplicar multas por trotinetes mal estacionadas" (6 December 2022): shared scooters are parked at the city's sharing points (pontos de partilha), and the operators are fined for those left elsewhere

map.title: Câmara Municipal do Porto's sharing points, on Porto Digital's urban platform (FIWARE)

source.title: Zarząd Dróg Miejskich w Poznaniu, "Zasady parkowania": since 1 April 2024 a shared scooter in the paid parking zones, from the Old Town to Jeżyce, Wilda, Łazarz, Ostrów Tumski, Śródka and Piotrowo, is left only at a Hop & Go point, and elsewhere preferably at one

map.title: Zarząd Dróg Miejskich w Poznaniu, "Punkty mikromobilności Hop & Go" (Google My Maps, on its page): its Hop & Go points and the zone where a shared scooter must be parked at one

source.title: Reykjavíkurborg, "Verklagsreglur um stöðvalausar hjólaleigur 2026" (in force since 4 February 2026): no faster than 10 km/h in its slow zones, school grounds and pedestrian streets among them; no parking in the areas it sets, as water protection areas, pedestrian streets and underpasses; and the places it sets for parking

map.title: Reykjavíkurborg, "Escooter_geofencing" and "Skilasvæði deilifarartækja" (open data, ArcGIS)

source.title: Rīgas dome, binding regulations No. RD-24-261-sn (27 March 2024, in force since 1 May 2024): a shared scooter may not be left in a no-parking zone, but at a parking place the city's map shows, nor ridden in a speed zone faster than its limit; the city publishes the zones on GeoRīga

map.title: Rīgas dome, "Elektroskrejriteņu izmantošanas nosacījumi" (open data, CC BY 4.0)

source.title: Hanse- und Universitätsstadt Rostock, "E-Tretroller & Elektrokleinstfahrzeuge in Rostock": under its agreements with the operators, a hired scooter's ride may not end in the no-parking zones, as parks, the Warnow's banks and the pedestrian zones, and the city is making parking places at their edges and at public transport stops

map.title: Hanse- und Universitätsstadt Rostock, "Abstellflächen für E-Tretroller": its marked parking places for e-scooters (open data, CC0)

source.title: City of Sacramento, "Motorized Scooter Safety & Law": park a shared scooter upright in one of the City's designated drop zones or at a public bike rack

map.title: City of Sacramento, Department of Public Works, "Verified Bike Racks Public Layer" (ArcGIS): its drop zones among the City's bike racks

source.title: City of Santa Monica, Shared Mobility Device Program Administrative Regulations (7 November 2025): devices are shut off or slowed to 1 mph on the Promenade, the Pier and Pier Bridge and in all City parks, and shared e-scooters also on the Beach Path, Ocean Front Walk and the rest of the beach zone, as the City's prohibited riding areas show; a ride ended in one of the City's designated drop zones costs $1 less. Both layers are the City's open data (ODC-By 1.0)

map.title: City of Santa Monica, "Mobility Prohibited Riding Areas" and "Shared Mobility Drop Zones" (open data, ArcGIS)

source.title: Seattle Department of Transportation, "Bike Racks & Parking": its bike and scooter corrals downtown, organized parking for shared bikes and scooters

map.title: City of Seattle, "Bicycle Racks" (Seattle GeoData, ArcGIS): its bike and scooter zones among the racks SDOT maintains

cities.authority: City of St. Albert, Open Data License

source.title: City of St. Albert, "Common E-Scooter Questions": the no-go zones on its Open Data Portal (City of St. Albert Open Data License), which the e-scooter companies geofence so that a scooter stops in them

map.title: City of St. Albert, "E-Scooter Restricted Zone" (open data, ArcGIS)

source.title: Stockholms stad, "Elsparkcyklar": about 700 parking places for e-scooters, and a scooter may be parked in any of the city's bicycle racks too; parking is forbidden along all the city's quays and at 13 places, as Gamla stan, Medborgarplatsen and Odenplan

map.title: Stockholms stad, Trafikkontoret, "Elsparkcykelplats": the city's parking places for e-scooters (open data, CC0)

source.title: Taupō District Council, "Rental E-Scooter Operational Areas" (CC BY 4.0): the areas where speed restrictions, parking restrictions and curfews apply to rental e-scooters, which the council may amend from time to time; 15 km/h in the town centre's reduced speed area, and no parking in its four no-parking areas

map.title: Taupō District Council, "E-Scooter Rental Operational Area" (map, ArcGIS)

source.title: Turun kaupunki, "Sähköpotkulaudat": park a scooter preferably in a place marked for scooters, painted on the ground or a rack, and never in a no-parking area; ride at most 10 or 15 km/h in the speed-limited areas, and not at all in the no-riding areas, which the city keeps up to date on its service map

map.title: Turun kaupunki, Palvelukartta, "Sähköpotkulaudat": the city's parking places, no-parking, speed-limited and no-riding areas for e-scooters, from its open map services (CC BY 4.0)

source.title: City of Vaasa, "New parking rules for electric scooters": from 15 June 2026 e-scooters may be parked only in designated parking areas in the city centre, Palosaari, Vöyrinkaupunki and Hietalahti; its 2026 permit terms add 10 km/h in the pedestrian centre, and no riding or parking on sports grounds and school and day-care yards

map.title: Vaasan kaupunki, "Rajoitusalueet_sahkopotkulaudat_view" (ArcGIS)

cities.authority: City of Vancouver, Open Government Licence – Vancouver

source.title: City of Vancouver, "Shared e-scooter system": the City places e-scooter parking stations throughout the service area, and a ride ends only at one. Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – Vancouver

map.title: City of Vancouver, "Shared E-Scooter Station" (open data, ArcGIS)

source.title: Vantaan kaupunki, "Geospatial dataset for the micromobility permit in Vantaa" (CC BY 4.0): 10 km/h for shared e-scooters in its low-speed zones, no riding or parking in its no-go zones, no parking in its no-parking zones, and its designated parking spots

map.title: Vantaan kaupunki, "Micromobility permit geodata" (ArcGIS Hub)

source.title: Västerås stad, "Res med elsparkcykel": the City's map shows where e-scooters may not be parked and where their speed is limited; park first at a designated place or in bicycle parking

source.title: District Department of Transportation, "District Shared Fleet Device Laws and Regulations": a shared scooter is parked on the sidewalk, between it and the kerb or at a bike rack or in-street corral, locked, leaving 3 feet clear, and not ridden on the sidewalk in the Central Business District; the zones where it may not be parked or ridden, or only slowly, are among the rules operators must keep to. The no-parking zones and the corrals are the District's open data (CC BY 4.0)

source.title: Stadt Wien, "E-Scooter, Elektro-Roller und Micro-Scooter – Regeln für das Fahren und Abstellen": since 19 May 2023 a rented e-scooter is parked first in a marked parking area, and not within 100 m of one elsewhere; there are no-parking zones, and in pedestrian zones an e-scooter rides only where cycling is allowed, at walking pace

map.title: Stadt Wien, "E-Scooter-Beschränkungszonen Wien" (open data)

source.title: Stadt Zürich, Dienstabteilung Verkehr, "Sharing Zonen": the zones sharing operators must keep in the city: in its no-riding zones a scooter is held to 4 km/h and a ride cannot end, in its no-parking zones a ride cannot end, and its parking zones are designated places to park; open data under CC0
